result:
The reader was right — fixed in `scenario.json`:

- Rewrote the request in a colleague's voice: "Set the estimate to 3 on the Apex team's offline sync issue assigned to Rae Ellison — she's on Chicago time and her status says 'Reviewing support queue'." All schema-like labels ("display name", "profile status", "timezone is …") are gone; "on Chicago time" and quoting her status read like something a user would actually write.
- Removed the F1 name-field decoy (full name "Rae Ellison" with display name "Rae E"). It was the source of the ambiguity: with wording natural enough to keep, that decoy could meet the request under a name reading, and pinning "display name" was exactly the constructed phrasing the reader flagged. Replaced it with a plain F0 decoy (assigned to Tessa Vaughn, same status/timezone/title/team).
- Kept the F8 display-name decoy ("Rae Ellison-Quinn"): a careful colleague would never take it for Rae Ellison, so the plain-name wording stays unambiguous, and it still tempts search-based solvers.
- Conditions re-split to the new phrases; query, seed, and write unchanged apart from the swapped decoy user/issue.
